html:
The main temple of Tenochtitlan, capital of the Aztec Empire. It was a pyramid with two shrines on top: one for Huitzilopochtli, god of war and the sun, and one for Tlaloc, god of rain. War and rain, tribute and farming, were the two things the city lived on.

The Mexica enlarged it seven times, each time building a new pyramid over the old one. At the rededication of 1487, under the ruler Ahuitzotl, large numbers of captives were sacrificed; how many is disputed.

After the fall of the city in 1521, the Spanish tore it down and built over it. The cathedral stands nearby. In 1978 electricity workers found a great carved stone of the moon goddess Coyolxauhqui. Excavations led by Eduardo Matos Moctezuma then uncovered the temple's earlier layers, and a museum now stands beside them in the heart of Mexico City.
